name: Scorpion & Sapphires
description: "Scorpion & Sapphires" — appearing on The Alternative Theory under the variant title "Scorpions & Sapphires," with the identical recording underneath — is one of the most evocatively titled records in That Boy Hi Hat's catalog, and the sound lives up to the name. The instrumental is nocturnal and cinematic, synth-driven with a bass-heavy pulse that moves like something gliding across hot pavement: dangerous but elegant, the scorpion in the sapphire light. It sounds like a late-night drive through a city that never quite sleeps — seductive, dystopian, and menacing, in the vein of the great neon-lit confessionals of dark trap. Arps flicker layered underneath the verses, an 808 sub bass pulses through the arrangement, and hi-hats tick with hypnotic restraint in the chorus. Vocal chops drift like smoke over the low end, pads swell throughout, and drums knock without breaking the spell. For fans of nocturnal rap and cinematic rap, the record recalls the patient menace of the catalog's darkest corners: mysterious, dark, and utterly controlled. That Boy Hi Hat delivers with a relaxed menace that never raises its voice, and the minor-key slink of the melody never brightens into major-key release. At 3:07, the record is all economy — no wasted motion. The mix is studio-polished but leaves the textures intact, with real depth in the low tones. It sits in the catalog beside the darker, more cinematic cuts, where the post-trap movement meets widescreen ambition, and the current wave of alternative rap has few records this comfortable in the dark. In an alt rap scene built on noise, "Scorpion & Sapphires" is That Boy Hi Hat proving that danger and beauty are the same instrument.
